entrypoints.summary: The report describes committing a new ValSetHeader through the signature/quorum path; practical abuse is conditional on significant compromise of a VotingPowerProvider on one participating chain.

affected_components.role: The report identifies this asset and recommends that its configuration and signature verifiers enforce voting-power distribution constraints.

relation_candidates.rationale: The report states that compromise of one chain can let it claim any voting power because no cap exists.
Aggregate voting-power quorum can be fulfilled by the compromised chain, allowing a single validator to commit a ValSetHeader with its own signature.
The report says the resulting header could be successfully committed on all chains.
The recommendation is to cap individual-chain voting power and require cross-chain participation constraints in signature verifiers.

impact.affected_asset: Multi-chain validator-set and settlement authority across participating chains.
impact.attacker_capability: Following significant compromise of one participating chain's VotingPowerProvider, supply enough claimed voting power to meet quorum with one validator signature and commit a new ValSetHeader.
impact.security_effect: Potential cross-chain acceptance of an attacker-controlled validator-set header.

causal_trace.summary: A VotingPowerProvider on one participating chain is significantly compromised, permitting that chain to claim arbitrary voting power.
ValSetDriver has no configuration to cap an individual chain's voting power, require contributions from a number of chains, or require a minimum contribution from each participating chain.

Because quorum is defined by aggregate voting power, the claimed weight from the compromised chain can satisfy minInclusionVotingPower, allowing a single validator to commit a new ValSetHeader using only its own signature.
The report states that the resulting ValSetHeader could be successfully committed on all chains, making the multi-chain system dependent on the weakest participating chain.

failure.operation: Acceptance of a single-validator-signed ValSetHeader after one chain supplies sufficient claimed aggregate voting power.

primary_invariant.statement: No individual participating chain should be able to satisfy a purported multi-chain validator-set quorum solely by supplying unbounded claimed voting power.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The quorum uses aggregate voting power and lacks per-chain caps, a required number of contributing chains, and minimum per-chain contributions.

quality.review_notes: This is a report-grounded finding, not a code- or execution-verified reproduction. The bundle contains no audited Solidity source, remediation diff, test, malicious header specimen, or runtime acceptance result. Exploitability is conditional on significant compromise of a VotingPowerProvider on one participating chain; the report marks the issue Closed as acknowledged, not as remediated.

remediation.invariant_restored: Quorum acceptance must enforce configured cross-chain voting-power distribution constraints rather than accepting quorum from an unbounded single-chain contribution.

state_context.attacker_state_setup: Significantly compromise a VotingPowerProvider on one participating chain so that chain can claim arbitrary voting power.
data_structure_invariants: Aggregate quorum must not be satisfiable by an unbounded contribution from one participating chain when multi-chain distribution is required.
Distribution controls should be evaluated by signature verifiers according to the report recommendation.

numeric_domains.attacker_constraints: The report states arbitrary claimed voting power is possible only after significant compromise of one chain's VotingPowerProvider.
numeric_domains.name: voting power

state_context.state_machine: A voting-power contribution is evaluated against minInclusionVotingPower for validator-set header commitment; no source-level state machine was supplied.
